questions.stem: A 13-year-old female patient visited OPD complaining of runny nose, backache, cough, fever and chills from the past 5 days. Many immunological mechanisms and mediators are involved in dealing with infections. Which of the following infections will be responsible for stimulating interferon alpha(α)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Viral infection
  • Interferon alpha and interferon beta for antiviral substances produced against viral infection.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 144

questions.stem: CASE1:- A 10-year-old male patient presented to OPD with a dog bite penetrating into deeper tissues and received anti-rabies immunoglobulin as a post-exposure prophylaxis initially.CASE-2: - A 2 years old male child receiving the oral polio vaccine in the pulse polio program in his primary schoolCase 1 and case 2, respectively, are examples of?

options.label: A
options.text: Active acquired immunity and passive acquired immunity

options.label: B
options.text: Passive acquired immunity and active acquired immunity

options.label: C
options.text: Primary acquired immunity and secondary acquired immunity

options.label: D
options.text: Secondary acquired immunity and primary acquired immunity

questions.answerText: Passive acquired immunity and active acquired immunity
questions.solutionHtml:
Passive acquired immunity and active acquired immunity
  • In passive acquired immunity, the antibody is directly received by the host. IgA-rich colostrum from mother to baby and immunoglobulin in post-exposure prophylaxis
  • Antigens enter the host cell in active acquired immunity, and antibodies are formed, as in the case of infection and vaccination.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 134

questions.stem: Innate immunity or inborn immunity is a first line of defence mechanism which is nonspecific and not associated with any memory. The innate immunity mechanism involves a variety number of cells and mediators. Which of the following is the mechanism of innate immunity except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Antigen-presenting cells

Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 134

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false regarding HLA complex genes?

options.label: A
options.text: HLA complex genes are located at the short arm of chromosome 6

options.label: B
options.text: MHC-1 is present in all nucleated cells and platelets & presents antigen to cytotoxic T cells in cell-mediated immunity

options.label: C
options.text: MHC-2 is present only in antigen-presenting cells, and they present antigen to CD4 T cells

options.label: D
options.text: All the above statements are true

questions.answerText: All the above statements are true
questions.solutionHtml:
All the above statements are true

Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 134

questions.stem: A 50 years old female presented to OPD with complaints of recurrent URTI upper respiratory tract infection. various immunological mechanisms play an essential role in defence towards a pathogenic condition. complement proteins are plasma mediators synthesised from the liver, which plays an important role in various immunological mechanisms. The complement system's ultimate role is forming a membrane attack complex. Complements forming membrane attack complexes are?
questions.solutionHtml:
C5,6,7,8,9
  • Complement proteins form membrane attack complex c 5 6 7 8 and 9, which results in cytolysis by humoral immunity mechanisms.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 142

questions.stem: Which of the following is the wrong pair regarding various cells in immunological mechanisms?

options.label: C
options.text: B cells- plasma cells and antibodies

questions.solutionHtml:
Natural killer cells- acquired immunity
  • Natural killer cells are large granular lymphocytes that play an important role in the mechanism of innate immunity.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg's Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 134

questions.stem: Mononuclear macrophages serve different functions in different tissues. All the following are correct regarding mononuclear macrophages except:
questions.solutionHtml:
B-cells-lymph node
  • B-cells are Lymphocytes, not macrophages.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 140

questions.stem: Which statement is true of the adaptive, but not the innate immune response?

options.label: B
options.text: It fights both viruses and bacteria.

options.label: C
options.text: Many cells coordinate together to mount it.

options.label: D
options.text: Pathogens have evolved to fight it.

questions.solutionHtml:
Receptors are highly specific
  • The adaptive immune system, also referred to as the acquired immune system, is a subsystem of the immune system that is composed of specialised, systemic cells and processes that eliminates pathogens by preventing their growth.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 537

questions.stem: Pattern Recognition Receptors (PRRs) are proteins capable of recognizing molecules frequently found in pathogens . Pattern recognition receptors (PRR) include:

options.label: C
options.text: CRP C-reactive protein AND MBL metallo beta-lactamase

questions.answerText: CRP C-reactive protein AND MBL metallo beta-lactamase
questions.solutionHtml:
CRP C-reactive protein AND MBL metallo beta-lactamase
  • Cells that typically have pattern recognition receptors include macrophages, dendritic cells, endothelial cells, mucosal epithelial cells, and lymphocytes.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 127

questions.stem: A vaccine is a biological preparation that provides active acquired immunity to a particular infectious disease. A vaccine typically contains an agent that resembles a disease-causing microorganism and is often made from weakened or killed forms of the microbe, its toxins, or one of its surface proteins. Which vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chickenpox
  • Live vaccines administered to a pregnant woman pose a theoretical risk to the fetus; therefore, live, attenuated virus and live bacterial vaccines generally are contraindicated during pregnancy.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 487

questions.stem: A 26-year-old male patient from India was diagnosed with Uncomplicated malaria. On thin smear examination, the species found was Plasmodium falciparum. Providing the same condition except the location being Africa another individual didn’t contract falciparum infection.Choose the correct response for the above racial immunity?

options.label: A
options.text: Acquired abnormality of red cells (sickling) prevalent in that area

options.label: B
options.text: Hereditary abnormality of red cells (sickling)in that area

options.label: C
options.text: Duffy negative RBCs are resistant to falciparum species

options.label: D
options.text: Duffy positive RBCs are resistant to falciparum species

questions.answerText: Hereditary abnormality of red cells (sickling)in that area
questions.solutionHtml:
Hereditary abnormality of red cells (sickling)in that area
  • Hereditary abnormality of red cells i.e., sickling is responsible for resistance to falciparum species in some parts of Africa and the Mediterranean coast. This is an example of racial innate immunity.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 81

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman primigravida woman at 26 weeks gestation comes for her first antenatal visit and as a protocol tetanus immunisation is suggested. Select the correct statement regarding immunisation?

options.label: A
options.text: Active immunisation of mothers during pregnancy improve the quality of passive immunity in infants

options.label: B
options.text: Active immunization of mothers during pregnancy improves the quality of active immunization in infants

options.label: C
options.text: Passive immunization of mothers during pregnancy improves the quality of active immunity in infants

options.label: D
options.text: Passive immunization of mothers during pregnancy improves the quality of passive immunization in infants

questions.answerText: Active immunisation of mothers during pregnancy improve the quality of passive immunity in infants
questions.solutionHtml:
Active immunisation of mothers during pregnancy improve the quality of passive immunity in infants
  • Immunization of pregnant women with TT is recommended for this purpose.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 81-85

questions.stem: A 40-year male resident of Bihar come with complaint of skin lesion mostly nodules, without loss of sensation, thickening of peripheral nerves with diminished sensation and burning or tingling sensation since many months. As an experiment, he was given some transfer factors in an attempt to treat the underlying condition. What kind of immunity this transfer factor represents?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adoptive immunity


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 86

questions.stemHtml: Which statement is incorrect regarding phenomena shown in image?

options.label: A
options.text: This is a crucial method of protection in immunosuppressive and immunodeficient individuals in whom vaccines are contraindicated

options.label: B
options.text: Once the herd immunity threshold has been reached, the disease gradually disappears from population

options.label: C
options.text: Herd immunity concept can apply to Tetanus

options.label: D
options.text: Herd immunity can be achieved by both vaccination and previous infection

questions.answerText: Herd immunity concept can apply to Tetanus
questions.solutionHtml:
Herd immunity concept can apply to Tetanus
  • Herd immunity concept does not apply to Tetanus. As the infection is acquired from the environment, rather than being passed from person to person, no Herd immunity is observed for tetanus. Therefore, every person needs to be individually protected.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 87

questions.stem: A vaccine is a biological preparation that provides active acquired immunity to a particular infectious disease. A vaccine typically contains an agent that resembles a disease-causing microorganism and is often made from weakened or killed forms of the microbe, its toxins, or one of its surface proteins. Conjugate vaccines are:
questions.solutionHtml:
N. meningitides Group B
  • Vaccines against serotype B meningococcal disease have proved difficult to produce as the capsular polysaccharide on the type B bacterium is too similar to human neural antigens to be a useful target. Also, the capsule of serogroup B (made up of sialic acid) is less immunogenic. It is also encephalitogenic due to the expression of similar cross-reactive antigens on neural cells.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 435-37, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 695-697

questions.stem: Innate, or nonspecific, immunity is the defence system with which you were born. It protects you against all antigens. Innate immunity involves barriers that keep harmful materials from entering your body. These barriers form the first line of defense in the immune response. All are true about innate immunity except?

options.label: A
options.text: Acts as the first line of defence

questions.solutionHtml:
Not affected by genetic influences
  • Innate immunity depends on the individual's genetic constitution. Homogenous identical twins exhibit similar degrees of innate.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 173-175, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 133-134

questions.stem: When complement is activated on a cell surface, the activation is limited by endogenous complement regulatory proteins, which include CD35, CD46, CD55 and CD59, depending on the cell. Complement which leads to the killing of an organism and protects us?
questions.solutionHtml:
C56789
  • C56789 is known as a membrane attack complex, which causes microbial lysis.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No.209-10, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 165-66

questions.stem: Active Immunity results when exposure to a disease organism triggers the immune system to produce antibodies to that disease. Active immunity can be acquired through natural immunity or vaccine-induced immunity. True about passive immunity:

options.label: A
options.text: Cannot be given with active immunity

options.label: C
options.text: It can be given before disease occurrence

questions.answerText: It can be given before disease occurrence
questions.solutionHtml:
It can be given before disease occurrence
  • Immunoglobulins should be given immediately after the exposure but before the disease occurrence. Passive immunity can be transferred between individuals by Serum therapy (antibodies).


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No.174, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 137
